signals.title: JPY/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Wage Data Surprise
signals.text: The G10 currency scorecard shows extreme divergence, with JPY leading all peers at +1.604% across 7 pairs while SEK lags at −0.644% across 2 pairs, generating a 2.247% spread. Japan July wage growth accelerated to +4.7% YoY, marking the strongest print since 1997 and reinforcing hawkish sentiment from BoJ officials while revised Q2 GDP printed at +1.4% YoY. In contrast, Sweden's Economic Surprise Index sits at −26.7, reflecting persistent macro disappointments. JPY holds this dominant outperformance despite a severe carry deficit, as BoJ 1.00% vs Riksbank 1.75% presents a 75bp yield headwind. Trade bias: Bullish JPY/SEK, driven by macro data divergence and BoJ normalization repricing. Catalyst: Riksbank rate decision on 24 Sep — 0% hike priced. Risk: Broad risk-on market rebound dilutes JPY safe-haven and carry-unwind support.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Macro Surge + Positioning Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 153.282, breaking decisively below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 158.72, 160.33, and 158.44. TONA OIS at 0.98% vs SOFR at 3.66% retains a +268bp carry advantage for USD, but spot price is aggressively decoupling from this spread following Japan's 4.7% wage growth surprise. COT data reveals extreme speculative short positioning in JPY with Leveraged Funds net short −111,297 contracts (pctl 2, z −2.18), while retail sentiment is 85% long USD/JPY, creating a severe contrarian unwind environment. Options markets confirm downside demand, with 25d Risk Reversals printing a sharp put skew of −2.55 and implied volatility trading at 7.2% against 11.8% 30-day realized volatility (VRP −4.6%). Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, driven by hawkish BoJ repricing and institutional short-covering. Catalyst: BoJ Policy Decision on 18 Sep — market bias leaning hawkish. Risk: US August CPI release on Friday prints significantly above expectations, reigniting Fed rate hike bets.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning Extreme + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7212, holding firm above its SMA20/50/200 cluster of 0.7144, 0.7048, and 0.6992. Leveraged Funds positioning is heavily stretched long at +50,250 contracts, sitting at the 94th percentile of its 52-week range (z +1.79). Retail sentiment strongly opposes this institutional stance, showing an extreme 90% short exposure and providing a powerful contrarian tailwind. Fundamental carry remains supportive via RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75% (+60bp spread; AONIA vs SOFR OIS −69bp), reinforced by Australia's positive Economic Surprise Index of +16.3. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD, supported by positive yield carry and institutional momentum against extreme retail fading. Catalyst: RBA Rate Decision on 29 Sep — hold expected. Risk: A sharp drop in industrial commodity demand depresses AUD fair value below its current model target.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Macro Catalyst
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3535, holding below its SMA20 level of 1.3556 while remaining anchored above the SMA50/200 support zone at 1.3461/1.3449. Leveraged Funds net long positioning stands elevated at +47,504 contracts (pctl 93, z +1.27), though WoW flows registered a reduction of 9,335 contracts. The options market signals substantial protection buying ahead of central bank events, with 1M implied volatility running at 11.0% against a 30-day realized volatility of 4.5%, generating a massive +6.5% Vol Risk Premium. Policy rate parity exists between BoE at 3.75% and Fed at 3.75% (OIS SONIA 3.73% vs SOFR 3.66% gives GBP a slight 7bp advantage), leaving price action sensitive to domestic fiscal and monetary headlines. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD, constrained by heavy options hedging and stalling speculative adds. Catalyst: UK Monetary Policy Report Hearings today at 13:15 UTC. Risk: BoE testimonies strike an unexpectedly dovish tone, triggering an unwind of crowded spec longs.
